tougaloo_backfill.convicted: Yes — disturbing the peace; $100 fine and a thirty-day suspended sentence
tougaloo_backfill.note: The library sit-in cost each of the nine about thirty-two hours in municipal custody. They were released on March 28, 1961 for court, convicted of disturbing the peace, fined $100 each and given thirty-day suspended sentences.

held_back.name: Lewell A. Cecil
held_back.why: The archive already holds Lewell A. Woods Jr., arrested in the same June 10, 1961 Jackson group. Lewell A. is not a name two men in one arrest group are likely to share, and the two forms come from separate passes over the catalog rather than from one list naming both. Creating this record risks publishing one man twice under a garbled surname. It needs the item-level catalog record to settle.

held_back.name: Jesse James Harris
held_back.why: Catalogued as a June 2, 1961 arrest, distinct from the July 6 Livingston Park arrest of Jesse Harris — who is already here as Jessie L. Harris. The source asserts they are two people but rates that only moderate, and flags a possible identity overlap needing biographical comparison. One SNCC organiser named Jesse Harris is documented for 1961. Not created.

rows.name: Janice LaJune Jackson
rows.description:
Janice LaJune Jackson was one of the Tougaloo Nine, the nine Tougaloo College students who walked into the whites-only main branch of the Jackson public library on March 27, 1961, asked for service and refused a police order to leave. They were arrested for breach of the peace, held about thirty-two hours, and released on March 28 for court. Each was convicted of disturbing the peace, fined $100 and given a thirty-day suspended sentence.

The Mississippi State Sovereignty Commission photographed each of them on arrest, and the Civil Rights Digital Library preserves the individual sit-in mugshots. The catalog does not name the jail that held them.

She is recorded in later life as Janice Jackson Vails.

The catalog establishes the arrest, the participation, and the individually identified police photograph, but not the court disposition, any transfer to Parchman, or the physical release date; those fields are unresolved pending county-jail, court, or penitentiary records.

He rode from Nashville to Jackson with the ten-person Greyhound group. The archival and secondary spellings of his name vary considerably — Widjonarko Tjokroadissumarto is the other form on record — and the version used here is the one the catalog gives.

cases.charges: Freedom Ride participation — arrested Jackson, July 29, 1961.
cases.convicted: Unresolved — the arrest is documented; the disposition is not established in the CRDL record
cases.sentence: Arrested 1961-07-29. The Civil Rights Digital Library establishes the arrest and the identification photograph but not the disposition, any transfer to Parchman, or the release date — unresolved pending court, jail, or penitentiary records.

rows.name: Margaret Winonah Beamer
rows.aka: Winonah Beamer Myers; Winonah Beamer; Winona Beamer
rows.description:
Margaret Winonah Beamer was arrested in Jackson, Mississippi, on June 9, 1961, for participating in the Freedom Rides and challenging segregation in interstate transportation — one of the arrests recorded by the Mississippi State Sovereignty Commission and preserved in the Civil Rights Digital Library. The catalog establishes the arrest, the participation, and the individually identified police photograph, but not the court disposition, any transfer to Parchman, or the physical release date; those fields are unresolved pending county-jail, court, or penitentiary records.

What is established for her, and is not established for most of the riders, is the length. She was held at the Mississippi State Penitentiary at Parchman for close to six months and served the term out rather than taking the appeal bond that released most of the others within weeks. She is reported to be the 1961 rider who served the longest full term.

The six months is recorded here as a duration and not as a pair of dates, because the Parchman admission and discharge dates are not established. The claim that hers was the longest full term rests on a secondary source rather than on the catalog.

She is recorded in later life as Winonah Beamer Myers, and shortened in the rosters to Winonah or Winona Beamer.

cases.charges: Freedom Ride participation — arrested Jackson, June 9, 1961; held at the Mississippi State Penitentiary at Parchman for approximately six months.
cases.convicted: Yes — the conviction appears to have stood through the full term; the judgment and any appellate history are not established
cases.sentence: Arrested 1961-06-09 and held at Parchman for approximately six months, serving the term rather than taking the appeal bond that freed most of the 1961 riders within weeks. The admission and discharge dates are not established, so the duration is recorded without them.
